Based on the above, how is P related to T if ‘P × Q + R ÷ S − T’?
questions.solution:
Given: P × Q + R ÷ S − T

​

Thus, P is T's mother’s mother or maternal grandmother.

questions.question: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some bags are purses. All purses are wallets. All wallets are sacks. Conclusions: (I) All purses are sacks. (II) Some wallets are bags.
questions.questionHtml:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if
it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the
statements.
Statements:
Some bags are purses.
All purses are wallets.
All wallets are sacks.
Conclusions:
(I) All purses are sacks.
(II) Some wallets are bags.
questions.solution:
Conclusions:

I. All purses are sacks → Follow (As some bags are purses, all purses are wallets and all wallets are sacks. As whole purses comes in wallets which whole comes in sacks, therefore it is true.)

II. Some wallets are bags → Follow (As some bags are purses and all purses are wallets. As whole purses comes in wallets and has some part common with bags, therefore it is true.)

∴ Here, Both conclusions (I) and (II) are follow.

questions.question: Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: No bench is chair. All sofas are benches. All tables are sofas. Conclusions: I. No table is a chair. II. Some sofas are chairs. III. All tables are benches.
questions.questionHtml:
Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if
they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the
statements.
Statements:
No bench is chair.
All sofas are benches.
All tables are sofas.
Conclusions:
I. No table is a chair.
II. Some sofas are chairs.
III. All tables are benches.

options.text: Only conclusions I and II follow
options.html: Only conclusions I and II follow

options.text: Only conclusions I and III follow
options.html: Only conclusions I and III follow

questions.solution:
Conclusions:

I. No table is a chair → Follow (As no bench is chair, all sofas are benches and all tables are sofas. As whole tables comes in sofas which whole comes in benches which cannot be chair, therefore it is true.)

II. Some sofas are chairs → Does not follow (As no bench is chair and all sofas are benches. As whole sofas comes in benches which cannot be chair, therefore it is false.)

III. All tables are benches → Follow (As all sofas are benches and all tables are sofas. As whole tables comes in sofas which whole comes in benches, therefore it is true.)

∴ Here, Only conclusions I and III follow.

questions.solution:
As M is common on both the dices, it is clear that T, A, P, and S are adjacent to it, and the remaining i.e. R will be opposite to it.

Opposite pairs:

questions.question: Each vowel in the word ‘SIMILAR’ is changed to the following letter in the English alphabetical order and each consonant is changed to the preceding letter in the English alphabetical order. How many letters are there in the English alphabetical order between the letter which is the second from the left end and the third from the left end in the group of letters thus formed?
questions.questionHtml: Each vowel in the word ‘SIMILAR’ is changed to the following letter in the English alphabetical order and each consonant is changed to the preceding letter in the English alphabetical order. How many letters are there in the English alphabetical order between the letter which is the second from the left end and the third from the left end in the group of letters thus formed?
questions.solution:
Given word S I M I L A R

Vowel → (+1)

Consonant → (-1)

 (-1) (+1) (-1) (+1) (-1) (+1) (-1)
Resultant R J L J K B Q

Thus, the new formed letter cluster → R J L J K B Q

Now, the number of letters are there in the English alphabetical order between the letter which is the second from the left end and the third from the left end: (Left end) R J L J K B Q (Right end)

Here, one letter i.e 'K' is between J and L.
